pr.title: Collapse the panel's pull requests from the header's count
pr.head: bf593c295551da0f8a76eb4bf81707d490e763f4

summary: Projector's panel sits above the Claude Code prompt. Its first line, the header, reads /projector on the left and, on the right, counts such as 2 pull requests · 1 question · 3 notices and how long ago the panel reloaded. Below the header come the pull requests the session's review and watch loops track, one row each, and then the inbox items: questions an agent asked and notices it posted.

Pull request #358 made the question and notice counts into buttons. Pressing one collapses that kind of item to a single line, such as - 2 questions, so a burst of notices cannot push the questions out of view. A long list of pull requests can push the items out of view the same way, but its count stayed plain text.

This pull request makes the N pull requests count a button too. Pressing it replaces the rows, and any open pull request drawer, with one line such as - 2 pull requests where the rows were, in the rows' default color. Pressing that line, or the count again, brings the rows back. The pull requests, the questions, and the notices collapse independently, and the choice persists across panel reloads.
The code now treats the three counts as one list of a new Section type, which is 'pr' or a kind of item, so the header's buttons and the collapsed lines are drawn from one place.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Section: something the header counts and can collapse, the pull requests ('pr') or a kind of item ('question' or 'notice').
  • panelCollapsed: the stored list of collapsed sections, kept in the plugin's state so it outlives a reload.
  • Drawer: the details a row or item opens under itself when pressed.
  • Expander: the one line, such as - 2 pull requests, that stands in for a collapsed section and expands it when pressed.

groups.title: The Section type
groups.kicker: One name for everything the header can collapse
intro: Before this change, the stored list of collapsed things held only kinds of item. Now it can also hold 'pr', so the type of that list widens to a new Section union.

checks.text: hooks/typecheck.sh enforces both: a probe assigning 'bogus' to a Section failed it, and so did a probe writing 'bogus' to the collapsed atom in fold.

groups.title: Drawing the header and collapsing the rows
groups.kicker: The render handler builds the counts, the buttons, and the collapsed lines from one list
intro: The panel is drawn by one ui.render handler in hooks/register.tsx. It used to compute the pull request count separately from the item counts, put it in the header's plain text, and draw buttons only for the item counts.

Now sectionCounts lists all three counts in header order. The header draws every non-empty count as a Button whose press calls fold, and a new expander draws a collapsed section's one-line stand-in. The pull requests' expander goes where their rows were, and the item kinds' expanders stay at the top of the items, as before.

checks.text: A section counts as collapsed only while the header shows a count for it. With no pull requests there is no count, so the rows cannot be hidden with nothing left to expand them from.

files.note: Replaces the item-only kindCounts with sectionCounts, makes the pull request count a Button, and hides the rows while pr is collapsed.

checks.text: fold filters the stored list to SECTIONS before toggling, so an unknown value from another module version drops out. The #358 module filters to item kinds and ignores a stored pr.
A header that counts anything is now a row of pieces, so a header with only pull requests is no longer a single Text. Only a header with no counts at all stays one Text.

A collapsed pull request's open drawer stays open in the drawer atom and reappears on expand. Its hotkeys belong to Buttons that are not drawn while collapsed, so they cannot act on the hidden drawer.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: A new test for the pull request count, and old header checks read through headerOf
intro: The new test presses count:pr and checks the collapsed line, its default color, that the header keeps counting, that the pull requests collapse apart from the questions and survive a poll, and that both the line and the count expand them.
Several older tests matched the header as one Text. Since a header that counts pull requests is now several pieces, they read it through the existing headerOf helper, which joins the pieces.

checks.text: claude plugin test . passes at this head: 152 pass, 0 fail.

files.note: Adds the collapse test and moves header assertions to headerOf.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: The user guide and the inbox plan describe the new behavior
intro: docs/plugins.md now says any count in the header collapses what it counts, where each collapsed line appears, and that the three collapse independently. The inbox plan, already completed, gains § 27 recording the change, its reasons, and the tests that cover it.

checks.text: The keyboard section of docs/plugins.md still says ctrl+x tab lands "onto its first line" and does not mention Enter on a count. With the pull request count now a button ahead of the rows, the ring may land on a count first on any panel that lists a pull request. Not reproduced; the test harness does not model focus order.
